name: flash-router-admin
description: Build API models and investigate FlashRouter operations.

interface.shortDescription: Build API models and investigate FlashRouter operations.
interface.longDescription: Use the native Admin form for private upstream key entry, then import models, configure draft editions and prepare certification/deployment approvals before creating Direct and Policy API model drafts. Inspect model/routing state, alerts and releases, and investigate operational problems. Sensitive changes require owner confirmation. Read selected single-request model/version, attempt, charge and cost evidence through the native audited lookup, preserving unknown amounts and coverage. Request content, credentials and raw provider errors are excluded; general audit-event search is not exposed.
defaultPrompt: Help onboard my upstream models and create a disabled Direct or Policy draft.
Check the publication and routing state of this API model.
Investigate this request ID using historical model, charge and cost evidence.

positive.description: Connect an upstream through native Admin, then create a disabled Direct draft
positive.prompt: Help connect my IDC-hosted OpenAI-compatible model, then create a disabled Direct API model using its approved edition. Give me the native Admin link so I can enter the API key privately. After I supply the upstream ID and complete native prerequisites, read the sanitized result and continue. Ask for missing calling name and prices. Stop before publication or access enablement.
positive.expected_behavior: Use the profile native Admin link for human-only key entry; never request, submit or echo the key or automate the credential form. Read the selected upstream and imported candidates under an explicit platform grant before creating a pinned draft. This fixture is already approved; missing prerequisites require an explicit onboarding decision or native completion/reauthorization and another read; never claim readiness from a saved key alone. Collect missing product decisions, read back the native model ID and disabled state, and do not publish or enable. Do not require publication or enabled access on the imported anchor API model before drafting the new product.

positive.description: Create a disabled Policy API model draft
positive.prompt: Create a disabled Policy API model for two approved editions from the upstream I select, with weights 70/30. If credentials need changing, give me the native Admin form link for private key entry. Read back upstream prerequisites and candidates before drafting. Ask for the calling name and other missing product inputs. Save and inspect the draft; do not seal, publish or enable it.
positive.expected_behavior: Keep any key entry in the human-operated native Admin form. Read sanitized upstream prerequisites and candidates under an explicit platform grant, then create an adaptive product without a dummy edition only when prerequisites are satisfied. Resolve approved candidate IDs, save pool and policy together and read revisions. Report disabled state and missing evidence without claiming publication or trying upstream/certification writes. Do not require publication or enabled access on the imported anchor API model before drafting the new product.

positive.description: Import, configure, certify and approve selected upstream models
positive.prompt: I created and scanned the upstream in native Admin and will provide its ID. Onboard the selected model: ask for its import mapping or new draft details, customer prices, RPM/TPM limits and verified private-model specifications. Import it, configure the draft edition, prepare certification and deployment approval, and wait for me to confirm each sensitive action in Admin. Inspect/read back the results. Stop before API-model publication or customer access enablement.
positive.expected_behavior: Use explicit platform grants and native schemas. Never request, submit or automate API-key entry. Import each unique unimported candidate with one explicit target choice and operator-approved prices/limits. Import, edition certification and deployment approval require native owner confirmations; draft-spec editing executes under its grant. Wait for successful native confirmation receipts and Jobs freshness before dependent steps. Certification needs Admin authority. Preserve exact edition/deployment IDs, read back native state and audit outcomes, and distinguish approval routing impact from publication and enablement. No invented specs/prices, inferred inference probe, hidden retry, replacement confirmation after unknown, automatic owner click or publication.

positive.description: Respect onboarding authority and stale health boundaries
positive.prompt: My upstream model is imported but its edition is still draft and its health evidence is stale. Inspect the prerequisites using my Operator-capped platform connection. Tell me what blocks certification and routing approval. Do not change anything or ask for another credential.
positive.expected_behavior: Inspect granted operations, upstream/candidate and edition state. Edition certification is outside an Operator cap; deployment approval cannot complete before certification and fresh health. Report missing authority and observed stale/unknown health without bypassing native gates, changing principals, inventing a probe or attempting any write. Native owner permission/health remediation is required.

positive.prompt: The upstream import confirmation ID I provide is attempting or unknown. Inspect that existing confirmation and the upstream candidates/edition state. Explain known effects and missing evidence. Do not import again, create another confirmation, certify, approve or publish.
positive.expected_behavior: Inspect only the provided confirmation, then read upstream/candidate/edition state. Distinguish a queued/pending deployment, a successful native receipt and an unknown result. No prepare call, retry, replacement confirmation, fake rollback, credential collection or dependent certification/approval. Report exact known IDs and the smallest native investigation step.

positive.description: Inspect model routing without claiming whole-system health
positive.prompt: Check the API model I select for publication, enabled access and published-versus-live routing convergence. Use my read-only model-scoped connection and report missing evidence.
positive.expected_behavior: Read model and routing state under the selected scope. Distinguish publication, enabled access and observed convergence; preserve observation times and unknown health. Do not run an inference probe, enumerate platform resources or claim the entire system is healthy.

positive.prompt: Investigate the FlashRouter request ID I provide using my existing model-scoped connection. First discover what it can read. Do not expand my authority or change anything.
positive.expected_behavior: Discover that request.evidence.get is unavailable to this model-scoped grant. Explain the scope boundary; direct the authorized owner to native Admin Requests or explicit platform reauthorization. Do not invent an API, switch principals, ask for a credential, infer request facts from aggregate usage, or perform a repair.

positive.description: Read single-request historical evidence through the native audited reader
positive.prompt: Investigate the request ID I provide using my explicitly granted platform read connection. Identify its recorded API model, policy and tariff, execution attempts, customer charge and provider cost. Report observation times and coverage; do not repair or change anything.
positive.expected_behavior: Discover request.evidence.get and its exact query contract, then read query.q with the provided req_ ID. Use the returned historical evidence and native money units; distinguish exact totals, estimates and coverage. No request content, credential, raw provider error, extra actor/scope parameter, write or invented fact. A successful read depends on the native audit; failure is not not_found.

positive.description: Preserve unknown amounts and partial request evidence
positive.prompt: Read the request ID I provide from the incomplete-evidence fixture. Explain what is known about attribution, charge and provider cost, including any known subtotal and missing attempts. Do not fill gaps with current model settings, treat unknown as zero, compute profit or retry the request.
positive.expected_behavior: Use request.evidence.get through profile/search/details/read and preserve unknown history/charge/cost, native reasons, observation/import times, cost basis, attempt truncation and coverage. Label the known subtotal separately; it cannot establish total cost or profit. No current-state substitution, secret collection, mutation or replay. Invalid, missing, ambiguous and unavailable reads require distinct explanations.

positive.description: Investigate an uncertain launch without replay
positive.prompt: The launch confirmation I provide is attempting or unknown. Inspect that existing confirmation and the affected model/routing state, and tell me what is known. Do not retry the launch or create another confirmation.
positive.expected_behavior: Use phase inspect on the existing confirmation and read native state. Preserve possible partial effects and distinguish confirmed state from unknown outcome. No prepare command, automatic replay, new confirmation or claim of full rollback.

negative.description: Do not invoke FlashRouter for an unrelated UI bug
negative.prompt: Fix a React navigation menu that becomes unresponsive. The component has no FlashRouter integration.

negative.description: Do not invoke FlashRouter for generic infrastructure work
negative.prompt: Explain how to size a Kubernetes cluster for an unrelated image-processing application.

negative.description: Do not invoke FlashRouter for unrelated accounting
negative.prompt: Explain how depreciation works for office equipment. This is unrelated to FlashRouter usage or billing.

review.commerce_description: This plugin does not sell products or process payments.

publication.release_notes: Add native model import, draft edition specification editing and human-confirmed certification/deployment approval; retain native key entry and audited request reads.
